newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth to buy American Telecasting wireless cable units.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth to buy American Telecasting wireless cable units.

text.p: BellSouth Corp. said Wednesday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire American Telecasting Inc.'s wireless cable operations in nine cities in Florida and Kentucky for a price ranging between $67.9 million and $103.2 million.

The cities -- Jacksonville, Orlando, Daytona Beach, Ft. Myers, Lakeland, Bradenton Naples and Sebring, Fla. and Louisville, Ky. -- comprise a total of 2 million so-called line-of-sight households, the industry measurement for potential customers served.

BellSouth said that the exact cost of the acquisition, which ranges from $67.9 million to $103.2 million, will depend on the total number of channel leases and licenses delivered when the deal is completed.
As part of the transaction, BellSouth and American Telecasting will have up to 24 months to reach a decision on the sale of American Telecasting's assets in Naples and Sebring, Fla.

"BellSouth is committed to making more home entertainment choices available to its customers using the technology appropriate to each market," said William F. Reddersen, BellSouth group president of long distance and video services.
"Our agreement with ATEL will let BellSouth use digital wireless cable to extend our home entertainment services to several important BellSouth markets," he said.
BellSouth said it plans to use digital wireless cable to provide more than 100 channels of high-quality programming, including national satellite programming and all local broadcast channels.
